To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

The 11.5% and 11% probabilities on 32°C and 34°C reflect residual uncertainty around exact peak timing and any brief shower activity, while the low odds on 35°C+ or sub-32°C outcomes mirror the narrow but well-defined forecast envelope. Traders are weighting the authoritative MSS guidance and ongoing dry conditions most heavily, with the market likely to stay sensitive to any afternoon model updates or real-time observations from Changi or other stations.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 2 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=lemd

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecasts from multiple models, including GFS, indicate clear skies, light southerly winds, and high pressure will drive strong daytime heating across Madrid's plateau today, supporting a peak near 35–36 °C under typical late-summer conditions. Official guidance and ensemble runs show limited variability, with minimal cloud cover or moisture to suppress temperatures, consistent with historical September maxima around 30 °C and the 36.4 °C record from 2014. Trader consensus reflected in the 70.5 % implied probability for 36 °C aligns with this model consensus, while the 20.5 % on 37 °C accounts for possible slight under-forecasting in afternoon observations. Updated model runs and official station data through the afternoon will refine the final daily maximum used for resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Clear skies, light southerly winds, and strong daytime solar heating under a stable high-pressure pattern are positioning Beijing’s September 2 high near 30–31 °C.** Multiple operational forecasts (GFS-based and local models) converge on a maximum of 29–32 °C, with the most probable values clustering at 30–31 °C—precisely where market-implied odds are highest (30 °C at 24.5 %, 31 °C at 50.5 %). 

September climatology shows an average high of ~28.7 °C, but the absence of significant cloud cover or precipitation today allows temperatures to exceed that baseline by 1–3 °C. Recent model runs have remained consistent, with only minor adjustments in the 30–32 °C envelope; this stability explains the tight distribution of probabilities and the low odds on outliers (≥33 °C or ≤29 °C). 

Official resolution will rely on the Beijing Meteorological Service’s maximum temperature reading for the calendar day. As the afternoon peaks and final observations are reported, any deviation from the 30–31 °C consensus would quickly shift the market, though current conditions and model agreement continue to favor that narrow range.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from numerical weather models and official sources positions 19°C as the most probable daily maximum for Cape Town on September 2, 2026, with 20°C a close second.** 

Multiple forecasts, including those aligned with South African Weather Service guidance and global models, indicate a daytime peak near 19–20°C (roughly 66–68°F) under mostly sunny to partly cloudy skies with moderate southerly winds. These conditions reflect typical early-spring climatology for the region, moderated by the cool Benguela Current and limited warm-air advection. Recent model runs show stable high pressure and no incoming fronts or heatwaves that would push temperatures notably higher or lower. 

Trader sentiment, reflected in the heavy weighting toward 19°C (51.5%) and 20°C (37.5%), aggregates these real-time meteorological signals and updated observational data. Lower probabilities for 21°C+ or 18°C and below align with the narrow uncertainty range in current guidance, which shows minimal model spread around the expected maximum. As the day progresses, any late revisions to afternoon observations or model adjustments could shift the final recorded high within this tight band.

eventMetadata.context_description: Consistent forecasts from multiple meteorological sources, including AccuWeather, local Shandong reports, and numerical models, project a high near 29–30°C for Jinan on September 2 under clear skies and light northeast winds, placing the outcome well above the 26°C threshold. Early September climatology in the North China Plain favors daytime maxima in this range when high pressure dominates, with minimal cloud cover and no precipitation expected to suppress insolation. Trader consensus at 96.5% for 26°C or higher reflects this strong model agreement and real-time observations showing temperatures already climbing steadily through the morning. A realistic challenge would require an unanticipated surge in low-level moisture or a faster-moving frontal boundary, though current guidance shows no such development through the afternoon peak.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast consensus points to a peak of 29–31 °C in Incheon/Seoul on September 3, with 30 °C holding the strongest market-implied probability.** Official guidance from the Korea Meteorological Administration and multiple global models shows partly cloudy to clear skies after recent rainfall, allowing daytime heating under moderate northerly to northeasterly flow that limits extreme warmth. Dew points in the low-to-mid 20s °C and light winds support efficient but not excessive insolation, aligning with early-September climatology where highs typically range 27–31 °C. Recent clearing after September 1–2 precipitation has removed cloud cover that previously capped temperatures, tightening the distribution around 30 °C while keeping a small tail for 32 °C or higher if mixing remains limited. Traders are weighting the latest model runs and historical analogs showing low likelihood of either strong cold advection or heat advection on this timeframe.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Amsterdam Airport Schiphol Station in degrees Celsius on 3 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eham

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.
